title: World Food Forum Youth Policy Board 2027-2028
organization: World Food Forum (WFF) Youth Initiative, Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations (FAO)
overview: A one-year (renewable once) volunteer board of 40 young people aged 18 to 35 who lead regional and thematic youth consultations on agrifood systems towards the 2028 FAO Regional Conferences. Open to high-school graduates who have completed or are enrolled in a bachelor's degree, nationals of an FAO Member State, with C1 English, about 25 hours a month and a weekly one-hour meeting.
duration: 1 year, with the possibility to reapply for a second year
deadline_text: Reported by secondary sources (Opportunity Desk, Opportunities for Africans): 30 November 2026, no time stated. The official WFF Youth Policy Board page still shows an "Open Call for Applications" (read 2 November 2026), but no deadline is shown on it or in the 2027-2028 Terms of Reference; the application form is an embedded Microsoft Form that automated readers could not load on 2 November 2026.
funding_details: The 2027-2028 Terms of Reference read on 26 October 2026 do not mention any stipend, payment or travel funding.
age_requirement: "Be between 18 and 35 years as of 30 April 2027"
experience_requirement: "Have demonstrated experience, knowledge or strong engagement in agrifood systems, policy advocacy and youth empowerment"; preference for experience in youth organisations or consultative youth processes
education_requirement: Graduated from high school and either completed or enrolled in a bachelor's degree programme at the time of application
nationality_requirements: Nationals of an FAO Member State (the DRC is listed among FAO's Member Nations on FAO's membership page, read 2 November 2026)
language_requirement: Spoken and written English at C1 level; fluency in other FAO official languages is an advantage
eligibility: Aged 18 to 35 on 30 April 2027
High-school graduate who has completed or is enrolled in a bachelor's degree
National of an FAO Member State
English at C1 level
Available for at least one weekly 1-hour meeting between 09:00 and 18:00 CET/CEST and about 25 hours per month
Not employed by FAO, not an immediate family member of an FAO employee, and not a current or former YSG or YPB member
documents_required: Shortlisted candidates submit a CV, a letter of recommendation and a two-minute video
application_process: Apply through the online form on the WFF Youth Policy Board page
Four rounds: secretariat review, committee shortlist (CV, recommendation letter, two-minute video), evaluation by the outgoing YPB, interview

title: World Food Forum Young Scientists Group 2027-2029
organization: World Food Forum (WFF) Youth Initiative, Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations (FAO)
overview: A two-year volunteer group of early-career researchers aged 18 to 35 who give scientific input to FAO's World Food Forum youth work and write a biennial report on an agrifood systems topic. Open to graduates and students of a graduate degree programme (master's or PhD) who are nationals of an FAO Member State, with good English and about 20 hours a month.
deadline_text: Reported by secondary sources (Opportunity Desk; Opportunities for Africans quoting "29 January 2027 23:59 CET (Rome time)"). The official WFF page says "The call for applications for the 2027-2029 YSG cohort is now open!" (read 26 October 2026) but does not show the deadline.
funding_details: The 2027-2029 Terms of Reference read on 26 October 2026 do not mention any stipend, payment or travel funding.
age_requirement: "Be between 18 and 35 years of age as of 31 December 2028"
experience_requirement: Candidates are scored "based on eligibility and experience"; the group expects postgraduate-level research and writing
education_requirement: "Applicants must have graduated or be enrolled in a graduate degree programme at the time of application"; specialised in a field relevant to FAO's work
nationality_requirements: Nationals of an FAO Member State (the DRC is listed among FAO's Member Nations on FAO's membership page, read 2 November 2026)
language_requirement: "Have demonstrated proficiency in spoken and written English"
eligibility: Graduated from or enrolled in a graduate degree programme
Aged 18 to 35 on 31 December 2028
National of an FAO Member State
Field relevant to FAO's mission
English proficiency; about 20 hours per month
Not employed by FAO and not an immediate family member of an FAO employee
documents_required: Shortlisted candidates submit a letter of recommendation and a two-minute video
application_process: Apply through the online form linked on the WFF Young Scientists Group page
Three rounds: Youth Initiative team review, FAO expert committee shortlist (recommendation letter and two-minute video), interview

title: WHO internship programme (headquarters and country offices)
overview: Internships of 6 to 24 weeks at WHO headquarters and offices worldwide. Vacancies are posted throughout the year and each has its own deadline.
deadline_text: "As internship opportunities are posted on a continuous basis, with each containing different requirements and application deadlines, we encourage you to check the internship page regularly" (WHO page, read 12 October 2026).
funding_details: WHO page: a living allowance is given to selected interns who need financial support, assessed through a declaration; medical and accident insurance is included.
age_requirement: At least 20 on the date of application
education_requirement: Enrolled in, or finished within the last 18 months, a university programme in a relevant field, with three years of full-time university study completed before starting
nationality_requirements: Valid passport of a WHO Member State (the DRC is listed among the countries of the WHO African Region on the WHO Regional Office for Africa page, read 2 November 2026)
language_requirement: Fluent in a working language of the office
eligibility: At least 20 years old
Enrolled in or recently finished (18 months) university studies, with three full-time years completed
Passport of a WHO Member State
Fluent in a working language of the office
No previous WHO internship and not related to WHO staff
application_process: Apply only through an internship vacancy notice on the WHO Careers site, using WHO's online recruitment system (Stellis)

title: African Union Youth Volunteer Corps (AU-YVC)
overview: Continental programme that recruits young African professionals, trains them and deploys them as volunteers for 12 months in an African Union member state other than their own. The 13th cohort call ran from 26 March to 26 April 2026.
deadline_text: 13th cohort: applications from 26 March to 26 April 2026 (11:59 pm EAT) on jobs.au.int. No 14th call was found on 2 November 2026: the au.int volunteer page still asks readers to watch for a call and gives no dates.
expected_next_cycle: No 14th call yet: the AU page (read 2 November 2026) still asks readers to "be on the lookout for an advertised Call for Applications on the AU Careers page and official social media platforms". The 13th call ran 26 March to 26 April 2026.
funding_details: Secondary sources describe a monthly stipend and accommodation; the amounts were not read on an AU page.
age_requirement: 18 to 35 at the time of completing the 12-month service
experience_requirement: At least one year of verifiable volunteer experience and one year of professional work experience
education_requirement: A post-secondary qualification (TVET, bachelor's or master's)
nationality_requirements: Citizen of an AU member state, living on the continent or in the diaspora (the DRC is listed on the African Union's member states page, read 2 November 2026)
language_requirement: At least one AU working language: Arabic, English, French, Kiswahili, Portuguese or Spanish
eligibility: Aged 18 to 35 when the 12-month service ends
A post-secondary qualification (TVET, bachelor's or master's)
At least one year of verifiable volunteer experience and one year of professional work experience
Available for 12 months and willing to live in another AU member state
documents_required: Professional CV on the African Union template
Letter of recommendation not older than 2 years
application_process: Apply on the AU careers portal, jobs.au.int
The African Union charges no application fee
